dedupe_keys.name: usfa statistical reports on fire departments and firefighters

description: This series of statistical reports describes the work of US fire departments and the risks to firefighters. It is published by the US Fire Administration, part of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, mainly from National Fire Incident Reporting System (NFIRS) data, with vital records and National Fire Protection Association survey estimates. Reports include the fire department overall run profile, which found that departments responded to 26,959,000 incident runs in 2020, 6 percent fewer than in 2019, broken down by incident type; the annual Firefighter Fatalities in the United States report, which identifies and analyses every on-duty firefighter death from 1986 to 2022; and topical reports on fire-related firefighter injuries for 2018 to 2020. Methodology papers explain how national estimates are built from NFIRS. Coverage is national. Reports are free to read online and download as PDF from a federal agency and are public domain. Caveats: NFIRS participation is voluntary and incomplete, estimates are scaled nationally, and data lag one to two years. Simulation uses: workload mixes, incident rates and responder risk figures for fire and emergency service capacity models. Related records: the NFIRS public data release (data-usfa-nfirs-public-data-release) gives the underlying incident records, and the USFA National Fire Department Registry (data-usfa-national-fire-department-registry) lists the departments.
